comment: Cross-language golden vectors for the commissioned safety binding. A producer must emit these exact canonical bytes; an independent verifier in a different language must accept every case in 'cases' and refuse every case in 'reject_cases' with the declared reason, evaluated against the declared verifier_context. Signed with the TEST-ONLY seeds below - never use them in production. The commissioning and provisioning seeds are deliberately distinct: a corpus sharing one key could not express wrong_authority at all.
canonical_form: ori-specs/gateway-mqtt-canonical-json/v1.md, numbers additionally constrained to the D-011 agreement zone
signed_over: canonical bytes of the 'binding' object, not the envelope
authority_rule: binding.signing_key is compared against configured anchors as raw key material before the signature is verified; signer_id is an audit label and is never an authority input
firmware_profile_comment: The mapping a firmware device may act on. Signed by the commissioning authority and bound to the binding hash, because a manifest reference proves only that firmware claims a relationship to a binding - a build system can embed a correct hash beside a wrong mapping.
envelope_comment: The wire wrapper around a signed document. Closed like everything else: signature encoding and decoded length are grammar, and an unknown field beside the signature is outside the signed bytes and therefore unauthenticated by construction.

cases.name: two_zone_site_correctly_bound
cases.note: Two clamps and two contactors, each pair bound by identity and proven by actuation. The two zones carry opposite commissioned mappings, so a verifier that derives one from a convention rather than reading it fails exactly one of them.

cases.name: pre_energisation_proof_accepted
cases.note: Terminal states proven at the terminals with a meter before the site load was first energised. Acceptable for autonomous actuation: the association is measured, not asserted.

cases.name: undemonstrated_zone_accepted_in_development
cases.note: Document is well-formed and accepted. The borehole zone's actuating profiles stay inactive and the runtime logs a consolidated WARNING; its non-actuating profiles remain available. The main zone is unaffected.

binding.reason: load could not be interrupted at commissioning

proof.reason: borehole pump serves a live ward; interruption refused by site

cases.name: revision_with_fresh_proof_accepted
cases.note: A recalibration changes `calibration_ref`, so the prior proof no longer establishes the binding and a fresh one is carried. `supersedes` names the canonical hash of the document it replaces.

reject_cases.name: transposed_binding
reject_cases.note: The contact was observed to open and the instrument still finds the load energised afterwards, because the clamp is on a different circuit from the contactor. This is the transposition case, and it is caught by the instrument's own load determination rather than by reading a threshold into a current value.

reject_cases.name: terminal_state_observed_contradicts_command
reject_cases.note: The contact was observed closed after a command to open the circuit.

reject_cases.name: proof_performed_on_an_idle_load
reject_cases.note: The load was not drawing before the open command, so opening it demonstrated nothing: an idle circuit reads the same on both sides of an actuation. A low reading after the command is not on its own evidence that this contactor controls this circuit.

reject_cases.name: proof_delta_within_the_sensor_noise_floor
reject_cases.note: The instrument reports the load gone, and the recorded current moved by 0.02 A against a declared noise floor of 0.05 A. A change the sensor cannot resolve is not a measurement, whatever the instrument says.

reject_cases.name: polarity_mismatch
reject_cases.note: `active_high` is false, so a de-energised coil is driven by a high GPIO level. The observation records a low level for the de-energised command, which contradicts the declared driver polarity.

reject_cases.name: outcomes_name_one_coil_state
reject_cases.note: Both circuit outcomes map to `de_energised`. A coil has two states, so one of the two observations is wrong.

reject_cases.name: terminal_state_contradicts_open_outcome
reject_cases.note: `open_protected_circuit` is `de_energised` while `de_energised_terminal_state` is `closed`. Both cannot be observations of the same channel.

reject_cases.name: capacity_above_sensor_full_scale
reject_cases.note: A 120 A capacity on a clamp that reads to 100 A describes a load the sensor cannot measure at all.

reject_cases.name: trip_point_above_sensor_full_scale
reject_cases.note: Capacity is comfortably in range at 25 A, and the release-owned multiplier of 5.0 puts the trip point at 125 A, beyond the clamp's 100 A full scale. A saturating sensor reports the hazard as a merely high reading, so the cutoff can never fire. This is the case a capacity-only bound misses.

reject_cases.name: signed_by_provisioning_authority
reject_cases.note: Genuinely signed by the provisioning authority, which is why the verdict is reachable at all: it is decided after the signature verifies, so a stranger cannot manufacture the event by naming that key over a forged signature. Refused because the commercial plane must not be able to move a trip point by raising a declared capacity.

reject_cases.name: signed_by_previous_commissioning_generation
reject_cases.note: The previous generation is verify-only for the binding already in force. A new binding must be signed by the current generation, or a compromised key would keep authoring bindings after rotation.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_is_not_a_commissioning_generation
reject_cases.note: Self-consistent - the document names the key that signed it - and that key is neither generation of the commissioning anchor.

reject_cases.name: anchors_are_identical_key_material
reject_cases.note: Both configured anchors are the same 32 bytes, so `wrong_authority` could never be reached and the separation the contract rests on does not exist. Refused at configuration load, before any document is verified.

reject_cases.name: replayed_binding_seq
reject_cases.note: `binding_seq` does not strictly exceed the accepted one.

reject_cases.name: supersedes_does_not_match_accepted
reject_cases.note: `binding_seq` advances but `supersedes` names a document that is not the one in force, so the chain does not connect.

reject_cases.name: actuator_replaced_without_fresh_proof
reject_cases.note: The revision moves the main contactor to a different GPIO pin and carries the previous proof unchanged. A new actuator does not inherit the mapping the previous one was proven to have.

reject_cases.name: undemonstrated_zone_under_hardened_posture
reject_cases.note: Same document as the accepted development case. Under production posture an undemonstrated zone cannot activate an actuating profile, and a runtime that quietly disabled the cutoff while reporting healthy is the worst available outcome, so startup fails.

binding.reason: load could not be interrupted at commissioning

proof.reason: borehole pump serves a live ward; interruption refused by site

reject_cases.name: duplicate_actuator_identity
reject_cases.note: Two zones claim the same contactor. Refused rather than resolved: there is no ordering preference and no nearest-match rule.

reject_cases.name: duplicate_sensor_id
reject_cases.note: One clamp bound into two zones with different actuators.

reject_cases.name: sensor_absent_from_declared_inventory
reject_cases.note: A binding may only name hardware the device declared.

reject_cases.name: declared_actuator_left_unbound
reject_cases.note: The device declares two actuators and the document binds one. Refused in hardened posture rather than silently leaving a contactor ungoverned.

reject_cases.name: wrong_device
reject_cases.note: A binding signed for one device must never be accepted by another.

reject_cases.name: bad_signature
reject_cases.note: Names the current commissioning key and is signed by someone who does not hold it. Key selection finds the named key and the signature is what refuses; no authority verdict is issued over an unverified document.

reject_cases.name: unknown_actuator_kind
reject_cases.note: `kind` is a closed vocabulary. An unrecognised kind is refused, never treated as the nearest known one.

reject_cases.name: reason_absent
reject_cases.note: `actor` and `reason` are structurally required, so a document missing either is a shape violation rejected before signature verification. There is no audit-specific verdict.

reject_cases.name: mapping_key_absent
reject_cases.note: The mapping has no default: a channel missing any of its three facts cannot be actuated.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_with_non_canonical_padding
reject_cases.note: A different spelling of the same 32 bytes: strict base64 accepts it and it decodes to the identical key. Only round-trip equality refuses it, and without that rule two implementations disagree about a document neither considers malformed.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_is_not_valid_base64
reject_cases.note: The signed body names a key that is not base64 at all. A verifier that raises here rather than returning a verdict has not refused the document.

reject_cases.name: signing_key_is_not_thirty_two_bytes
reject_cases.note: Well-formed base64 that is not an Ed25519 public key. Length is part of the grammar, so this never reaches key selection.

reject_cases.name: supersedes_is_not_a_digest
reject_cases.note: `supersedes` is either null or a lowercase sha256 digest; a free string would make the revision chain unverifiable.

reject_cases.name: actuator_kind_is_an_array
reject_cases.note: A closed vocabulary tested by membership before its type is checked raises rather than refuses: arrays and objects are unhashable. Every vocabulary in this contract has the same shape, so one of them is carried as the representative case.

reject_cases.name: proof_method_is_an_object
reject_cases.note: The same defect on a different vocabulary, and on the field that selects which shape the rest of the proof must have.

reject_cases.name: noise_floor_declared_as_a_boolean
reject_cases.note: JSON separates booleans from numbers and some languages do not: in Python True is an instance of int, so a naive numeric check accepts this. A verifier that does is reading a threshold out of a flag.

reject_cases.name: signer_id_is_whitespace_only
reject_cases.note: A field carrying no information is not a field that was supplied, and an empty signer in an audit record is worse than an absent one because it looks answered.

reject_cases.name: unknown_sensor_field
reject_cases.note: The closed grammar reaches nested objects. A sensor field a consumer does not read is refused rather than dropped.

reject_cases.name: unknown_observation_field
reject_cases.note: An observation is a closed shape too. An extra field in a proof is a claim about how the proof was performed, and an ignored claim is worse than a refused one.

reject_cases.name: identity_shape_does_not_match_actuator_kind
reject_cases.note: A local-GPIO identity on a firmware channel names an actuator that does not exist, and would leave active_high unread on a device with no pin.

reject_cases.name: gpio_level_recorded_for_a_firmware_channel
reject_cases.note: A pin level is meaningless for a channel with no pin, so recording one is a shape error rather than an ignorable extra.

reject_cases.name: one_sided_sensor_reading
reject_cases.note: Readings are paired: a before with no after cannot show a change, and a verifier that skipped the delta rule on a missing field would silently accept the weaker proof.

reject_cases.name: superseded_derivation_field_present
reject_cases.note: `contact_type` is the field this contract exists to make unrepresentable. Unknown keys inside a zone are refused so a stale safety field cannot be silently ignored by a consumer that does not read it.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_carries_an_unknown_field
envelope_reject_cases.note: A field beside the signature is outside the signed bytes, so it is unauthenticated by construction. Ignoring it lets an intermediary add content a careless consumer might read.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_absent
envelope_reject_cases.note: An unsigned document is not a weakly signed one.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_without_its_algorithm_prefix
envelope_reject_cases.note: The wire encoding is `ed25519:<base64>`; a bare base64 string does not say what algorithm produced it.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_is_not_valid_base64
envelope_reject_cases.note: Refused by the grammar rather than by a decoder throwing inside verification.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_is_the_wrong_length
envelope_reject_cases.note: Ed25519 signatures are 64 bytes. A value that was never a candidate authenticator is malformed rather than a failed authentication.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_signature_with_non_canonical_padding
envelope_reject_cases.note: The same 64 bytes spelled differently. The rule that applies to a public key applies to a signature for the same reason.

envelope_reject_cases.name: envelope_binding_is_not_an_object
envelope_reject_cases.note: The wrapper names one document; a string is not one.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_carries_an_unknown_field
envelope_reject_cases.note: The same rule as the binding envelope, on the shape a firmware device actually receives. A field outside the signed bytes is unauthenticated by construction whichever document it accompanies.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_signature_is_not_valid_base64
envelope_reject_cases.note: Refused by the grammar rather than by a decoder throwing inside verification, on the constrained consumer where that distinction matters most.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_signature_with_non_canonical_padding
envelope_reject_cases.note: The same 64 bytes spelled differently, in the profile envelope.

envelope_reject_cases.name: profile_envelope_signature_absent
envelope_reject_cases.note: An unsigned profile is not a weakly signed one.

firmware_profile_cases.name: profile_matches_the_accepted_binding
firmware_profile_cases.note: The device holds the mapping itself, signed by the commissioning authority and bound to the binding hash. A runtime and a device that both verify this object cannot disagree about which coil state opens the circuit.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_mapping_disagrees_with_the_binding
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Correct binding hash, inverted mapping. This is the case a manifest reference cannot catch: the hashes match and the device drives the opposite coil state. Only carrying the mapping inside the signed object makes it detectable.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_names_a_different_binding
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: The mapping is right for a document that is not the one in force. The sequence still parses, so the refusal is the binding check rather than the grammar.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_binding_hash_is_malformed
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: `binding_hash` is a lowercase sha256 digest. A free string would make the tie between a profile and the binding it came from unverifiable.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signing_key_is_malformed
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A key that is not 32 bytes of strict base64 is refused by the grammar, before any key can be selected.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_for_another_channel
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A profile is scoped to one channel on one device.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signed_by_the_provisioning_authority
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Same authority rule as the binding, and decided the same way: after the signature verifies, so a build system cannot commission a channel by signing its own profile and cannot manufacture the verdict either.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_for_another_device
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A profile signed for one firmware device must never actuate another, the same rule inbound commands already enforce.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_with_an_unknown_field
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: The profile is a closed shape. An unrecognised key is refused rather than ignored, so a stale mapping field cannot ride along unread.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_bad_signature
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Names the current commissioning key and is signed by someone who does not hold it. Exercises the profile's own signature stage, which the binding corpus cannot cover on its behalf.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signed_by_the_previous_commissioning_generation
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Rotation applies to a profile exactly as it does to a binding: the previous generation verifies and does not sign. Reported as superseded rather than unknown, because dismissing it at key selection would describe our own rotated key as a stranger and hide that the profile was once legitimately signed.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_anchors_are_identical_key_material
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: A collision involving the previous generation is as fatal as one involving the current: if either commissioning anchor is the provisioning key, the separation the contract rests on does not exist for profiles either.

firmware_profile_reject_cases.name: profile_signing_key_is_not_an_anchor
firmware_profile_reject_cases.note: Self-consistent and signed by a key that is neither configured anchor, so no candidate can be selected and no signature is attempted.
